Market Segmentation The data center market can be segmented into three core segments: network infrastructure, storage, and servers. Network infrastructure refers to the interconnected hardware and software systems that enable communication and data transfer within and beyond the data center environment. Storage encompasses not only the physical media used to store data but also the architectures that structure and safeguard it. Servers, the backbone of data centers, are specialized computers that process requests and deliver Data Center Market Report – LLNL-TR-2013901 4 the stored data. Together, these segments form the foundation of modern data centers, supporting a wide range of digital services [7]. Among these segments, network infrastructure plays a particularly critical role in ensuring seamless communication within data centers. It connects servers, storage devices, cloud services, and other network equipment, enabling high-performance data transfer and reliable operations. This segment includes both hardware components, such as switches and routers, and software solutions. A well-functioning network infrastructure is essential for ensuring scalability, efficiency, and reliability in data center environments, especially as demand for cloud services and edge computing continues to grow [4] [8] [9]. Key Challenges The growth of the data center market is primarily constrained by power limitations and supply chain challenges. Power, in particular, is emerging as the critical bottleneck for the development of large-scale data centers [5]. According to Deloitte, data center power usage is expected to double by 2030, making energy efficiency a top priority for new sites [4] [6]. The demand for computing power is projected to grow by 16% annually from 2025 to 2028, driven largely by generative AI and other data-heavy technologies. Non-AI computing needs are also expected to increase as businesses continue to adopt cloud solutions for their cost efficiency and flexibility [5]. Geographical growth in the data center market is heavily influenced by access to scalable power markets and favorable regulatory environments, including tax incentives. In the United States, partnerships with regional transmission organizations (RTOs) such as PJM Interconnection and Midcontinent Independent System Operator are expected to play a key role in expanding data center capacity. Leading companies like Meta and Google are collaborating with power and utility providers to address future energy demands. For instance, Meta has partnered with Entergy for site planning in Louisiana, while Google is working with Intersect Power to develop future power infrastructure and with AES to secure power for data center expansions in Ohio and Texas [6]. Globally, the United States continues to dominate the data center market, but growth is expected in international markets around the world. Regions outside the US with access to renewable energy, like Nordic countries, are particularly expected to see growth. Cheap energy paired with the availability of alternative energy sources provide data centers with opportunities for co-located energy redundancies to mitigate grid bottlenecks, power reliability and sustainability concerns
